stem: Mice are fed a harmless protein together with cholera toxin as adjuvant. Several days later, secretory IgA against the protein is found in their intestinal secretions.
oneliner: Mice fed protein + cholera toxin adjuvant → secretory IgA in gut secretions → where is the antigen first sampled?
ask: At which site does the gut IgA response to the fed antigen begin?

options.A: Subcapsular sinus of a mesenteric lymph node
options.B: M cells in the epithelium over Peyer patches

whyNot.A: Lymph nodes receive **antigen already carried from the gut**, after sampling at the epithelium
whyNot.C: The spleen handles **blood-borne** antigen, not a fed one
whyNot.D: Site of **T-cell negative selection**, not response to ingested antigen
whyNot.E: Home to **long-lived plasma cells**, not the first antigen contact

answer: M cells over Peyer patches (gut-associated lymphoid tissue)
why: **M cells** in the follicle-associated epithelium take up luminal antigen and pass it to **Peyer patch** dendritic cells and B cells. **TGF-β** and Th cell help drive **class switching to IgA**. IgA plasma cells then secrete **dimeric IgA**, which crosses the epithelium as **secretory IgA**.

idea.rule: Mucosal IgA begins with M cells passing luminal antigen to Peyer patch lymphoid follicles.
also: Dimeric IgA is joined by a J chain and carried across epithelium by the poly-Ig receptor
Secretory component protects IgA from digestion
Oral polio vaccine induces gut IgA
Oral cholera and rotavirus vaccines also work through gut IgA

stem: Investigators want a drug that speeds renewal of the small-bowel lining, which is replaced every few days. In tissue sections, dividing cells are found only at the base of the epithelial glands, and their daughter cells move upward to the villus tip.
oneliner: Drug to speed small-bowel lining renewal + dividing cells at the base of glands + cells move up to villus tip → which structure to target?
ask: Which structure must the drug act on to increase epithelial turnover?

whyNot.B: Permanent **mucosal and submucosal folds** that enlarge surface area; the **dividing cells** sit elsewhere
whyNot.C: Mucus-secreting cells that **no longer divide** once on the villus, while the dividing cells lie at the base
whyNot.D: Absorptive cells that are **already differentiated** and are shed at the tip
whyNot.E: Apical **projections of enterocytes**, not dividing cells

why: Stem cells in the **crypts of Lieberkuhn** divide constantly, and their daughters differentiate while moving up the villus, to be shed from the **tip** after about 3-5 days. A drug that changes turnover must act on these **dividing crypt cells**.

idea.rule: The small-bowel lining renews from dividing stem cells in the crypts, so turnover depends on crypt cells.
also: Chemotherapy and radiation cause diarrhea by killing dividing crypt cells
Paneth cells at the crypt base secrete lysozyme and defensins
Villus enterocytes live only a few days before being shed from the tip
Celiac disease shows villous atrophy with crypt hyperplasia
